questions.question: Which of the following Rajiv Gandhi National Sadbhavana Awards was conferred on Ustad Amjad Ali Khan?
questions.solution:
Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, the legendary Sarod maestro, was conferred with the 21st Rajiv Gandhi National Sadbhavana Award. This award recognizes individuals for their outstanding contribution towards promoting communal harmony, peace, and goodwill.

Note: He is one of the most celebrated musicians of the Senia Bangash Gharana.

questions.question: Ustad Vilayat Ali Khan is a maestro in ________.
questions.solution:
Ustad Vilayat Khan was a world-renowned Sitar maestro belonging to the Imdadkhani Gharana (Etawah Gharana). He is credited with developing the 'Gayaki Ang' style, which enables the sitar to mimic the nuances of the human voice.

Fact: He famously turned down the Padma awards, stating that the selection committee was not competent enough to judge his music.

questions.question: __________ is often touted as Tansen of the 20th century, this musical genius blended the best of classical music and created a unique style of his own.
questions.solution:
Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan of the Patiala Gharana is often described as the Tansen of the 20th century. He was a master of the Khayal, Thumri, and Bhajan genres and was known for his incredible three-octave range.

Legacy: His voice was so versatile that he even sang for the classic film Mughal-e-Azam.

questions.question: Papanasam Ramayya Sivan was an Indian composer of which music style?
questions.solution:
Papanasam Sivan was a prolific Indian composer and singer of Carnatic music, often referred to as Tamil Thyagayya. He composed over 2,000 songs, many of which are staples in contemporary Carnatic concerts.

Context: He was also a celebrated composer for Tamil cinema in its early years.

questions.question: Alla Rakha is famous for playing which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
Ustad Alla Rakha was a legendary Tabla player of the Punjab Gharana. He is best known for his long and fruitful collaboration with Pandit Ravi Shankar, which helped popularize Indian classical music in the West.

Note: He was the father of another world-famous percussionist, Ustad Zakir Hussain.

questions.question: Which award was started by the Government of Madhya Pradesh in 1980 to the exponents of Hindustani classical music?
questions.solution:
The Tansen Samman was established by the Government of Madhya Pradesh in 1980. It is a prestigious national award given annually to eminent personalities for their contribution to Hindustani Classical Music.

Background: The award honors the memory of Tansen, one of the 'nine gems' in Akbar's court.

questions.question: Arvind Parikh, a Padma Bhushan awardee, plays which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
Arvind Parikh is a renowned Sitar player and a disciple of Ustad Vilayat Khan. He is unique for being both a highly accomplished musician and a successful businessman.

Award: He was honored with the Padma Bhushan in 2018 for his lifelong dedication to the Imdadkhani Gharana.

questions.question: Umayalpuram K Sivaraman is an eminent musician associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
Umayalpuram K. Sivaraman is a colossus in the field of Mridangam, the primary percussion instrument of Carnatic music. He is known for his technical brilliance and for innovating the design of the instrument to improve its tonal quality.

Recognition: He has been awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, the Padma Vibhushan, and the Sangeetha Kalanidhi.

questions.question: Which television channel presents the IMMIES Awards every year with an aim to reward the best talent in the Indian music industry?
questions.solution:
The IMMIES (Indian Music Memorial Awards) were presented by MTV India. The awards were launched to recognize and reward excellence across various genres including Indipop, Film Music, and Classical Music.

Note: It was one of the most popular televised music award ceremonies in India during the early 2000s.

questions.question: Pandit Ram Narayan was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
Pandit Ram Narayan is widely recognized as the musician who popularized the Sarangi as a solo concert instrument. Before him, the Sarangi was primarily used only as an accompanying instrument for vocalists.

Award: He is a recipient of the Padma Vibhushan.

questions.question: By which of the following state governments is the Tansen Music Festival organised?
questions.solution:
The Tansen Music Festival (Tansen Samaroh) is organized annually by the Government of Madhya Pradesh (specifically the Academy of Music and Art). It takes place near the tomb of Tansen in Gwalior.

Significance: It is one of the oldest and most prestigious music festivals in India, attracting performers from all over the world.

questions.question: MG Music Awards is presented annually by which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The MG Music Awards (Music Awards of Nagaland) is an annual event presented by the state of Nagaland. It aims to encourage local musicians and promote the diverse contemporary and traditional music scene of the region.

Context: Nagaland is often called the 'Land of Festivals' and has a very rich musical culture.

questions.question: Buddhadev Dasgupta is famous for playing which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
Buddhadev Dasgupta was a distinguished maestro of the Sarod, belonging to the Shahjahanpur Gharana. He was known for his deep research into the technicalities of the instrument and his scholarly approach to music.

Recognition: He was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and the Padma Bhushan.

questions.question: Padma Bhushan awardee, Ustad Sabri Khan played which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
Ustad Sabri Khan was a master of the Sarangi and a key figure of the Sainia Gharana. He was instrumental in bringing international attention to the Sarangi, performing at various prestigious global venues.

Note: He was known for his mastery over Taan and his soulful rendering of ragas.

questions.question: Sangeet Kala Acharya Award is given by which organisation every year since 1993?
questions.solution:
The Sangeet Kala Acharya Award is presented annually by the Madras Music Academy. It is given to senior musicians and teachers who have made significant contributions to the field of Carnatic music through teaching and performance.

Note: The Music Academy is also famous for its Marghazhi season festival.

questions.question: Annapurna Devi is associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
Annapurna Devi was a legendary performer of the Surbahar (a bass sitar). She was the daughter of Ustad Allauddin Khan and was known for her immense musical depth, although she spent much of her life in seclusion.

Teaching: She was the guru to masters like Pt. Hariprasad Chaurasia and Pt. Nikhil Banerjee.

questions.question: Harivarasanam award is given in the field of music by which of the following state governments?
questions.solution:
The Harivarasanam Award is presented annually by the Government of Kerala. It honors individuals who have made exceptional contributions to the fields of music, secularism, and universal brotherhood.

Origin: The award is named after the famous hymn 'Harivarasanam' recited at the Sabarimala Temple.

questions.question: Tarun Bhattacharya, who was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2018, is known for playing which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
Tarun Bhattacharya is a world-class maestro of the Santoor and a disciple of Pt. Ravi Shankar. He is credited with introducing the 'Mankas' (fine-tuners) to the Santoor, which helped in easier and more precise tuning.

Style: He represents the Maihar Gharana and has innovated the playing technique to include the Meend (slur).

questions.question: Which Indian musician and sitar player is the founder of the National Orchestra of India ?
questions.solution:
Pandit Ravi Shankar, the Bharat Ratna awardee and Sitar maestro, founded the National Orchestra of India (Vadya Vrinda). He was a pioneer in creating orchestral compositions for Indian instruments, blending traditional ragas with ensemble arrangements.

Note: He served as the conductor for All India Radio's National Orchestra.

questions.question: Who among the following was the youngest recipient of the Sangeetha Kalanidhi awarded by the Music Academy in 1947?
questions.solution:
Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer, often hailed as the 'Pitamaha' (patriarch) of modern Carnatic music, became the youngest recipient of the prestigious Sangeetha Kalanidhi title from the Madras Music Academy in 1947 at the age of 39.

Legacy: He was the guru to many legendary singers, including M.S. Subbulakshmi.

questions.question: Which Indian singer wrote ‘Raag Sarita’?
questions.solution:
Pandit C.R. Vyas (Chintaman Raghunath Vyas) was an eminent Hindustani vocalist and composer who wrote the book 'Raag Sarita'. He was a master of three gharanas: Kirana, Gwalior, and Agra.

Contribution: He composed many Bandishes under the pen name 'Gunijan'.

questions.question: Which of the following personalities is a Padma Shri awardee folk singer from the state of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.solution:
Ajita Srivastava is a famous folk singer from Uttar Pradesh who was awarded the Padma Shri for her contribution to preserving the Kajri folk music tradition of Mirzapur.

Note: Kajri is a popular genre of semi-classical songs sung during the rainy season in North India.

questions.question: The Nandi Award for Best Male Playback Singer was instituted by which state in the year 1977?
questions.solution:
The Nandi Awards are the highest award for excellence in Telugu cinema, theater, and television, presented by the Government of Andhra Pradesh. The award for Best Male Playback Singer was first introduced in 1977.

Fact: Legendary singer S.P. Balasubrahmanyam holds the record for the most Nandi Awards in this category.

questions.question: Sangeet Natak Akademy Awardee Sulochana Chavan was a famous ________ singer.
questions.solution:
Sulochana Chavan was an iconic Indian singer known for her mastery over Lavani, the traditional folk music of Maharashtra. She was often called the 'Lavani Samradni' (Queen of Lavani).

Recognition: She received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and the Padma Shri for her vibrant contribution to folk music.

questions.question: The renowned ghazal singer Girija Devi was born in ________.
questions.solution:
Girija Devi, known as the 'Queen of Thumri', was born in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh. She was a legendary exponent of the Banaras Gharana of Hindustani Classical Music.

Note: She was instrumental in elevating the status of semi-classical genres like Thumri, Dadra, and Tappa.
